label: Rust developer tools
scope: Principle: a developer tool is software that software developers use while building, testing, debugging, shipping or operating software. The test is who uses it and for what: if its main users are developers doing development work, it is on topic; if it is an app for some other audience or activity that merely happens to be written in Rust or run in a terminal, it is not. Illustrations only (not exhaustive): on topic are things like linters, build and test tooling, code search, version-control helpers, editor or language tooling, and tooling for AI coding agents; off topic are things like an end-user app for media, chat or personal finance, even with a CLI. When the description is ambiguous, read the README and apply the principle.

Fossil MCP is a Rust-based static code analysis and quality toolkit for developers, finding dead code, clones, and scaffolding through an MCP server and CLI.
Runner is a developer tool that orchestrates multiple AI coding agents in shared terminal-based missions.
lowfat is a Rust CLI developer tool that filters and condenses command and file output for AI coding agents, reducing noise and token usage during software development.
Markplane is a developer-focused project-management and AI coding-assistant tool that stores tasks and plans in repositories and integrates with editors, Git, and MCP.
Onmark is a screenplay-to-video authoring and rendering tool for creating films, aimed at content creators and agents rather than software developers doing development work.
Orbit is a Rust terminal developer dashboard/workspace for monitoring systems and integrating developer tools, primarily used by software developers.
